counter_evidence.note: Site is a retail/compounding pharmacy, not a clinic. It has a 'Dermatology' item page pitching compounded topical formulas for acne/rosacea/pigmentation/anti-aging, but this is a pharmacy dispensing compounded creams a provider prescribes — not a spa/clinic performing injectables, lasers, facials, or any hands-on aesthetic procedure. No skin, body-contouring, nail, or lash service is administered on-site.
counter_evidence.quote: From acne and rosacea to pigmentation and anti-aging treatments, compounding allows for customized combinations of active ingredients tailored to each patient’s skin.

counter_evidence.note: Same pattern for 'Hair Restoration' — a compounded topical product line, not a clinical hair-restoration procedure (PRP, transplant) performed in-house.
counter_evidence.quote: Hair restoration often requires a combination of ingredients and consistent use over time.

prior_reason_rebuttal: Prior verdict said 'Retail pharmacy — not a medspa/aesthetics clinic.' This still holds under the new criteria: the brief explicitly lists 'pharmacy' as a NON_CLINIC_BUSINESS example. The site's own item catalog (dermatology, hair-restoration, dentistry, weight-loss, hormone therapy, peptides, ketamine, low-dose naltrexone, sexual wellness, veterinary/pediatric compounding) is entirely a compounding-pharmacy product menu fulfilled by an outside prescriber (Elizabeth Magriby, NP of 'Renew Med'), not services performed by this business. Nothing on the site describes an in-house injectable, laser, facial, body-contouring, nail, or lash service — it is medication fulfillment, not aesthetic treatment delivery.
proposed_markdown_reason: Retail and compounding pharmacy (vaccines, prescription transfers, compounded medications for hormone/weight-loss/dermatology/hair-loss conditions dispensed on a provider's prescription) with no in-house aesthetic procedures — a pharmacy, not a clinic or spa.
